title: Stop ProfileRepositoryImpl.updateProfile silently swallowing tutor Cloud-Function write failures
rule: EH-2/EH-3 (typed errors must reach a boundary as values, no log-less catch) + Nygard lens (retry-assumption mismatch across facade implementations)

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)

/// When a tutor session is active ([activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider] !=
/// null) the outbox facade is wrapped by a [TutoredWriteRouter]

} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)

} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded.

why: ProfileRepositoryImpl wraps every _syncEngine?.pushLearnerProfile(...) call in a blanket catch(_) {} (createProfile:104-109, updateProfile:157-161, self-heal:321-336), on the premise that 'local write already succeeded (offline-first)' and the push will retry later. That premise only holds when _syncEngine is the durable OutboxSyncWriteFacade. Per sync_providers.dart:75-78, when a tutor session is active, _syncEngine is instead a TutoredWriteRouter that turns pushLearnerProfile into a one-shot, non-retryable Cloud Function RPC (tutorEditProfile). When that RPC fails (network drop, CF timeout, or the tutor's grant expiring mid-session), the failure is discarded: updateProfile still returns its local model as if the push succeeded, so the tutor's own local mirror shows the rename/mode/avatar change permanently while the owner's actual Firestore profile was never touched — a silent, non-retryable divergence between what the tutor sees and what actually persisted, with zero error surfaced. This also makes editProfileFlow's dedicated 'on TutorWriteException catch' (profile_edit_delete_actions.dart:46) dead code: repo.updateProfile can only ever let StateError or DuplicateProfileNameException (line 134) escape to its caller, and editProfileFlow doesn't catch the latter at all, so even a same-account name collision on the Edit flow throws unhandled — unlike ProfilePickerScreen's own separate rename dialog, which does catch DuplicateProfileNameException. profile_edit_delete_actions_test.dart exercises neither path (zero references to TutorWriteException or DuplicateProfileNameException in the whole file).
recommendation: Only swallow pushLearnerProfile failures when the underlying facade is genuinely durable/retryable (OutboxSyncWriteFacade); let a TutorWriteException-shaped failure propagate (or convert it to a typed Result the caller must handle) so editProfileFlow's existing catch becomes reachable and can tell the tutor the edit didn't save. Add a catch for DuplicateProfileNameException in editProfileFlow mirroring profile_picker_screen.dart's _showRenameDialog.
acceptance_criteria: ProfileRepositoryImpl no longer unconditionally swallows pushLearnerProfile failures when the sync facade is the tutor-routed (non-durable) path
editProfileFlow catches DuplicateProfileNameException and shows the existing profileNameTaken feedback, matching profile_picker_screen.dart's rename dialog
New regression test: a failed tutor-routed pushLearnerProfile surfaces a user-visible error from editProfileFlow (currently unreachable code path)
New regression test: updateProfile throwing DuplicateProfileNameException from the Edit dialog shows an error instead of throwing unhandled
mergedFrom: Guard ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile's cloud-sync push the same way create/update/ensureDefaultProfile do
